asOf: Market data as of 23 Oct 2026 close (screener.in); BCL Industries and Gokul Refoils read 26 Oct 2026 intraday, Vijay Solvex 21 Oct 2026 close
basis: Royal Oils & Foods: FY26 audited figures combining the proprietorship's first half and the company's second half, with valuation at the ₹200 Cr pre-money. Peers: FY26 (year to Mar 2026) annual results from screener.in (consolidated where available; Gujarat Ambuja Exports and Vijay Solvex standalone) and market cap in late Oct 2026. Peer multiples are computed on FY26 figures, not TTM. EV uses gross debt for every company.

companies.name: Royal Oils & Foods Ltd
companies.note: Groundnut-oil refiner at Gondal, Rajkot (85–90% groundnut), expanding from 70 to 260 TPD; valued at the ₹200 Cr pre-money.

companies.name: AWL Agri Business Ltd
companies.note: Formerly Adani Wilmar. India's largest branded edible-oil company (Fortune, Kings), sells groundnut oil among others; it is the sector's scale benchmark.

companies.name: Gokul Agro Resources Ltd
companies.note: Gujarat edible-oil refiner (main plant at Gandhidham; Vitalife, Mahek, Zaika). Like the subject, it runs a high-volume, thin-margin refining model.

companies.name: Gujarat Ambuja Exports Ltd
companies.note: Gujarat agro-processor: corn starch, soya derivatives, feed, cotton yarn and edible oils. A diversified regional peer.

companies.name: BCL Industries Ltd
companies.note: Bathinda-based edible-oil refiner (Homecook) with a large grain-ethanol distillery business; a mid-size refining peer.

companies.name: Vijay Solvex Ltd
companies.note: Rajasthan mustard-oil crusher and refiner (edible oils, vanaspati, de-oiled cake). A small-cap peer with a market cap close to the subject's valuation.

companies.name: Gokul Refoils and Solvent Ltd
companies.note: Gujarat (Sidhpur) seed processor, solvent extractor and refiner that also sells groundnut and cottonseed oils; the closest listed Gujarat model in size.

dims.name: Product / technology
dims.why: Royal Oils refines bought-in crude groundnut oil (85–90% of its mix); its distillation plant is still planned. AWL and Gokul Agro run multi-oil, multi-plant refining with vanaspati and specialty fats, and Gujarat Ambuja adds corn-starch derivatives.

dims.name: Customers and concentration
dims.why: Six or seven customers take Royal Oils' whole output, and exports go on 7–14 day credit after arrival with no advance. Listed peers sell through dealer networks, retail and institutions across many buyers.

dims.name: Entry barriers
dims.why: A 70 TPD groundnut refinery is small, licensable plant in a crowded Saurashtra cluster. AWL's brand and national distribution and Gokul Agro's port-based import refining at scale are far harder to copy.

dims.name: Distribution / reach
dims.why: Royal Oils sells business-to-business to a handful of buyers plus exports and has no stated retail network. AWL (Fortune) has pan-India FMCG reach, and Gokul Agro sells nationally under Vitalife, Mahek and Zaika.

dims.name: Scale of operations
dims.why: Royal Oils had ₹518 Cr revenue on 70 TPD of refining capacity, against ₹2,366–74,731 Cr for peers. Even at 260 TPD it stays below the smallest peer. Gokul Agro ran its refineries at about 82% in FY26 and is adding 46% capacity.

dims.name: Management and governance
dims.why: Royal Oils moved from a proprietorship to a company on 1 Oct 2025, so restated combined financials are still needed for the IPO. The desk's related-party review and its check of the ₹65 Cr subsidy are pending. Peers have multi-year listed disclosure records.

dims.name: Growth runway
dims.why: Capacity rising from 70 to 260 TPD (3.7x) underpins the company's ~₹27 Cr FY27E PAT, against ₹10.4 Cr in FY26, but that figure is a company estimate. Gokul Agro has compounded sales at 31% over three years and is executing a ₹430 Cr capex, while AWL's FY26 PAT fell 15%.

dims.name: Raw-material sourcing
dims.why: Royal Oils buys crude groundnut oil from small mills around Gondal. That puts it in the heart of the groundnut belt but exposes it to a single seasonal crop, without crushing integration. AWL and Gokul Agro source imported crude oils at scale through ports, and Vijay Solvex and Gokul Refoils crush their own seed.

dims.name: Brand strength
dims.why: Royal Oils has four registered brands, but its output goes largely to a few bulk and export buyers. Fortune is the category's leading national brand, while Gokul Agro and BCL (Homecook) have regional brand franchises.

Royal Oils is the smallest in the set, at about a fifth of Vijay Solvex's revenue.
Among the pure edible-oil refiners (AWL, Gokul Agro, Vijay Solvex, Gokul Refoils: 0.9–2.9%), Royal Oils' 3.4% is the highest.

Shares are illiquid until listing, and the IPO first needs restated combined financials.

barriers.name: Location in the groundnut belt
barriers.note: Gondal sits among Saurashtra's crude groundnut oil mills, giving Royal Oils short supply lines. Many local refiners share the same advantage.

barriers.name: Refining capacity and capex
barriers.note: At 70 TPD, today's plant is small and replicable. Moving to 260 TPD adds scale, but large peers' capacity is far bigger.

barriers.name: Buyer and export relationships
barriers.note: Six or seven repeat buyers take all output, which gives the company sticky volume. The same concentration makes it a vulnerability.

barriers.name: Brand franchise
barriers.note: Royal Oils has four registered brands, but sales are largely bulk and export. Consumer pull is not yet a moat against Fortune or regional brands.

barriers.name: Working-capital access
barriers.note: Refining needs bank lines for crude-oil inventory, and Royal Oils has ₹25.0 Cr of cash credit today. Equity from this round strengthens access; smaller entrants find this harder.

barriers.name: Licences and approvals
barriers.note: FSSAI and factory approvals for an edible-oil refinery are standard and do not restrict new entrants materially.

ahead: Royal Oils' EBITDA margin of 3.4% in FY26 is above every pure edible-oil peer: AWL 2.9%, Gokul Agro 2.8%, Vijay Solvex 1.5% and Gokul Refoils 0.9%.
Its PAT margin of 2.0% compares with 0.4–1.5% for the same pure refiners.
Planned capacity growth of 3.7x (70 to 260 TPD) is proportionally larger than any peer's announced expansion; Gokul Agro is adding 46%.
It is a groundnut specialist (85–90% of its mix) at the source of supply in Gondal, a niche the palm and soya-led large peers do not focus on.
behind: Royal Oils is the smallest in the set by far: FY26 revenue of ₹518 Cr against ₹2,366 Cr for the smallest peer (Vijay Solvex) and ₹74,731 Cr for AWL.
Six or seven customers take its whole output, while listed peers sell through dealer, retail and institutional networks.
Debt/equity of 1.58x is the highest in the set (peers 0.11–1.06x), and its net worth is only ₹18.0 Cr.
FY26 combines a proprietorship and the company, so there is no clean prior-year comparison, and restated financials are still needed.
watch: Commissioning of the 260 TPD capacity, and whether second-half FY27 sales reach about twice the first half, as the ~₹27 Cr FY27E PAT requires.
Restated combined financials and the desk's related-party review.
Verification of the stated ₹65 Cr subsidy (about ₹6.5 Cr a year).
Broadening of the customer base beyond six or seven buyers, and progress of the distillation plant toward the targeted 3.5–4.5% PAT margin.
valuation: At the pre-money, price/book is 11.1x against a peer range of 0.6–4.1x, and EV/EBITDA is 13.0x against a peer median of about 10.3x.
